Test niche proportions against an outcome

Source: R/niches.R
testNicheOutcome.Rd

Computes the proportion of each image's cells in each niche and tests every niche against a two-level outcome with a Wilcoxon or t-test.

Usage

testNicheOutcome(
  spe,
  nicheUnweighted,
  nicheWeighted,
  outcomeCol,
  test = c("wilcox", "ttest"),
  subject = NULL,
  cellID = "cellID",
  imageID = "imageID"
)

Arguments

spe

A SummarizedExperiment (e.g. a SpatialExperiment) with a cell ID, an image and the outcome for every cell in colData.

nicheUnweighted, nicheWeighted

Named cell-to-niche vectors, as returned by runNicheIdentification().

outcomeCol

Name of the per-image outcome column in colData(spe). It must have exactly two levels (subset your data to two conditions first) and a single value per image: repeated measures and mixed models are not supported. An error is raised otherwise, before any computation.

test

"wilcox" or "ttest".

subject

Name of the colData(spe) column identifying the subject (for example the patient) each image comes from, or NULL. If given, every image must belong to one subject and every subject must contribute only one image, as in runColocalisationModels(). With NULL this cannot be checked, and a message says so.

cellID, imageID

Names of the colData(spe) columns holding a unique cell ID (matching the names of the niche vectors) and the image each cell is in.

Value

A list with testUnweighted, testWeighted (one row per niche) and propUnweighted, propWeighted (per image niche proportions, to pass to nicheProportionBoxplot()).

Details

The estimate is the difference in the niche proportion for the second level of the outcome compared with the first (alphabetical order for text, factor order for factors), for both tests, as in runColocalisationModels(). For test = "wilcox" this is the Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the shift in location. Each image is one observation, so every image must come from a different subject if subject is given.

Examples

data(lungSubset)
data(lungCellTypeTree)
data(lungConfList)
niches = runNicheIdentification(lungSubset, lungCellTypeTree, lungConfList,
    r = 50, k = 6)
#> Computing unweighted LISA curves...
#> Generating local indicators of spatial association.
#> Computing weighted LISA curves...
#> Generating local indicators of spatial association.
#> Clustering niches...
res = testNicheOutcome(lungSubset, niches$nicheUnweighted,
    niches$nicheWeighted, outcomeCol = "disease_status", subject = "subject")
res$testWeighted
#>    niche    estimate statistic     p.value      p.adj
#> 1 niche4 -0.35213399        25 0.007936508 0.04761905
#> 2 niche6  0.13213213         5 0.150793651 0.37142857
#> 3 niche2  0.06735556         6 0.222222222 0.37142857
#> 4 niche1  0.10960504         7 0.309523810 0.37142857
#> 5 niche5  0.01701702         7 0.309523810 0.37142857
#> 6 niche3  0.00000000        12 1.000000000 1.00000000
